pinterest.title: Sand Ceremony Script With Sample Wording Your Celebrant Can Read Word for Word
pinterest.description: A sand ceremony script in three parts: the celebrant introduces the ritual, you pour, and the celebrant closes the moment. The couple need say nothing at all. The closing line from our classic version: "Look at what you have made. Two colours, one vessel, and every layer still there to see." Plus sample sand ceremony wording in several tones and a fill-in template to send your celebrant. Read the full guide.

pinterest.title: What You Need for a Sand Ceremony: Vessel, Carafes and Contrasting Sand
pinterest.description: A unity sand ceremony needs very little: one clear keepsake vessel, a small carafe for each person pouring, sand in contrasting colours, a small table, a funnel and a lid. Clear glass shows the layers, and a narrow neck slows the pour and keeps it neat. Choose shades that read clearly side by side, such as ivory and sea blue. Seal the vessel the same day so the layers do not shift. Read the full guide.

pinterest.title: Sand Ceremony Script for a Beach or Destination Wedding
pinterest.description: On a beach, a gentle breeze can lift a fine stream of sand straight off the table. Before you settle on the setting, ask the venue or local council about wind, who seals the vessel, and whether sand may be taken from the shore. Keep the table low and heavy. Our beach script ends: "Wherever you live, this will remind you of the light, the salt air and the people who travelled to stand here with you." Read the full guide.

slides: A sand ceremony asks very little of you on the day, which is exactly why the words around it matter.
Every script works in three parts: the celebrant introduces the ritual, you pour, and the celebrant closes the moment.
"Look at what you have made. Two colours, one vessel, and every layer still there to see. May your life together always have room for you both."
Where it goes: after the vows and rings, just before the pronouncement. Or straight after the welcome. Your celebrant sets the final order.
A sand ceremony is symbolic, so it sits beside the legal words of your ceremony and never takes their place.
With children: give each child their own colour and a carafe small enough to hold in one hand. Let them pour first, then pour your colours over the top.
On a beach, ask the venue or local council about wind, sealing the vessel and whether sand may be taken from the shore.
Planning a ceremony far from home? Message us to talk it through with a Wedded Advisor. Link in bio.
instagram_carousel.caption:
Two small carafes, one glass vessel, and a pause in the ceremony where nobody has to speak.

Our new guide, Sand Ceremony Script With Sample Wording, gives your celebrant something to read word for word: an introduction for your guests, the direction for the pour and the closing words. There is original wording in several tones too: short, romantic, secular, for a ceremony of faith, with children or a blended family, with parents, for a beach or destination ceremony and for a vow renewal.

A few lines from the scripts:
"Take your time. There is no right way to do this, only yours."
"Two colours, now one. Keep it close."
"Not a beginning this time, but a continuation. May the next layer be as rich as the ones before."

What to set on the table:
- One clear keepsake vessel. Clear glass shows the layers.
- One small carafe per pourer. Carafes with a lip pour more cleanly than jars.
- Sand in contrasting colours, such as ivory and sea blue, or blush and charcoal.
- A small table draped in linen, plus a funnel and a lid to seal the vessel.

Do a full run at the rehearsal with the actual vessel and carafes.

A sand ceremony is symbolic, so it sits beside the legal words of your ceremony and never takes their place. Ask your celebrant which legal lines they will say, and build the pour around them.
